title: Framer vs WordPress: Hosted Visual Site Building or Flexible Publishing?
description: Compare Framer and WordPress by editing workflow, hosting model, content structure, extensibility, SEO controls, ownership and maintenance. Current prices and product limits are not independently verified; validate the exact setup before migrating.

features.name: Operating model
features.tool1: Evaluate the hosted visual site-building workflow and its publishing constraints for the intended site.
features.tool2: Evaluate the content-management and hosting setup, including who maintains updates, plugins and infrastructure.

features.name: Content and editorial workflow
features.tool1: Test templates, reusable components, redirects, publishing and how nontechnical editors update pages.
features.tool2: Test posts, pages, taxonomies, media, roles and editorial review using the actual publishing model.

features.name: SEO and portability
features.tool1: Verify canonical URLs, redirects, metadata, sitemap, structured data and export options for the current product.
features.tool2: Verify canonical URLs, redirects, metadata, sitemap, structured data, plugin dependencies and export options.

features.name: Performance and reliability
features.tool1: Test key page templates, image delivery, caching and production behavior under realistic content.
features.tool2: Test the theme, plugins, caching, hosting and database under realistic traffic and content.

features.name: Maintenance and control
features.tool1: Confirm the vendor's current hosting, plan limits, backups, access and exit options.
features.tool2: Plan hosting, core/theme/plugin updates, backups, security and incident response.

features.name: Total cost
features.tool1: Include plan, add-ons, design work, migration and any limits that affect the site.
features.tool2: Include hosting, themes, plugins, maintenance, backups, developer time and migration.

verdict: Neither Framer nor WordPress is a universal winner. Choose by the work that must be completed, test the current product and plan with representative tasks, and verify important features, privacy terms and current pricing directly with the vendors. This comparison does not publish independently verified ratings or price claims.

faqs.question: Which is better, Framer or WordPress?
faqs.answer: There is no universal winner. Define the task and constraints, then compare both against the same acceptance criteria and evidence.

faqs.question: Are current prices and ratings verified here?
faqs.answer: No. Current prices, plan limits and independent rating datasets are not verified in this comparison. Check official documentation and request a dated quote.

faqs.question: How should I run a fair comparison?
faqs.answer: Use the same input, workflow, users and expected outcome. Record pass, partial pass, fail or unknown and attach current vendor evidence for material claims.

faqs.question: What is often missed in a software comparison?
faqs.answer: Migration, data portability, permissions, integration failures, ongoing maintenance, support and renewal terms. Include these in the total-cost and risk assessment.
